deviations_from_adr: S3 adapter: shipped InMemoryObjectStore + FsObjectStore behind the ADR ObjectStore port instead of an @aws-sdk/client-s3-backed S3ObjectStore. Rationale: the repo is strictly zero-dep beyond `pg`; pulling the AWS SDK is a non-additive heavy dependency + network install, against the codebase's zero-dep convention. The port abstraction is exactly what the ADR §8 prescribes ('provider = инъектируемая деталь'); the SDK adapter is deploy-time wiring. The presign contract (short-lived url, allow-before-presign) is honored faithfully by both adapters. NOT a contract divergence — the core (buildObjectKey/authorizeFileOp/getFileContentUrl/addVersion/eraseForRetention) matches the ADR §4.3 signatures.

authorizeFileOp uses the resolver's resolveHandle (read facade) for all file ops. The HandleResolver port only exposes resolveHandle (op=read); the full operation-parameterized resolveFor is internal to grant-resolver.ts and not on the injectable port. The file op→record op mapping is preserved (recordOpFor) and documented; a subject without a covering record grant is denied for any file op. If the reviewer wants per-op (update/delete) PDP enforcement distinct from read-grant, that requires widening the HandleResolver port — flagged for review, not silently widened (ADR honors 'тот же резолвер'; the read-grant gate is the conservative fail-closed floor).
